author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (given name first). All specialties render on one page; veterinarians holding no specialty do not appear.
acceptance_criteria: A GET request to /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name
Each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, each shown by full name with given name before family name (for example Helen Leary)
All specialties render on one page with no pagination controls
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the page; the page lists specialties and their holders, not the full veterinarian roster
Specialties, and the veterinarians within each specialty, render in a stable order across requests
The page is reachable by its address alone: this slice adds no navigation entry and no link from any other page
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged) — this is a read-only view
Any navigation entry or cross-page link to the new page (deferred to a possible follow-up request)
notes: Open question recorded in docs/prd.md REQ-SPC-001: whether every specialty stored (including one held by no veterinarian, shown with no holders) must appear, or only specialties at least one veterinarian holds. Seeded specialties (radiology, surgery, dentistry) are all held, so both readings coincide today; design-time source-of-specialties choice (derive from vets vs. read the specialties store) rests with system-design-expert. Full name derives from Vet extends Person (firstName, lastName).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A read-only Specialty directory in the vet feature package, following the established server-side-rendering pattern (ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf) and the controller-per-feature-package pattern (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). The genuinely new design ground is the source-of-truth decision, recorded in ADR 2026-08-22-specialty-directory-derived-from-veterinarians: the page is DERIVED FROM VETERINARIANS (grouping held specialties from the cached VetRepository.findAll()), not read from a specialties store. This is the narrowest reading of the requirement — only held specialties appear, which the seeded data (radiology, surgery, dentistry, all held) renders identically to the store reading, and no acceptance criterion requires an unheld specialty to appear. The handler is a NEW package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package injecting VetRepository; no SpecialtyRepository is introduced. Domain terms per docs/ubiquitous-language.md: Specialty (held by zero-or-more Veterinarians), Veterinarian (Vet is the code short form).
integration_points: GET /specialties.html served by the new SpecialtyController; reachable by address only — no nav entry added to fragments/layout and no link from any other page (acceptance criterion 6)
Data source is the cached VetRepository.findAll() (the non-paged, @Cacheable("vets") method) — the same read path and cache the vet list uses; no new repository, query, or store read
Template lives under templates/specialties/ and uses the shared fragments/layout fragment, mirroring templates/vets/vetList.html but with no pagination block

patterns.description: SSR list template using the layout fragment and #{} message keys; the specialty page follows this shape minus the pagination div
package-private @Controller with @GetMapping returning a view name and populating the Model; SpecialtyController mirrors this
Vet.getSpecialties() already returns specialties sorted by name; the handler inverts this vet->specialties mapping into specialty->holders

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002: the build-time test walks templates and compares every locale bundle's keys; a new #{} key absent from any of the eleven bundles fails the build
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing message keys — #{specialties} for the heading/column, #{vets} for the holders column, #{none} for the empty case; only introduce a new key if unavoidable, and then add it to every locale bundle under src/main/resources/messages/

risks.risk: 'Stable order across requests' (acceptance criterion 5) — VetRepository.findAll() returns rows in unspecified order
risks.mitigation: Impose ordering in the handler: specialties by stored name, veterinarians within each specialty by a deterministic key (e.g. last name then first name); do not rely on database or Set iteration order

risks.risk: View model shape — passing a raw Map<String,List<String>> to the view trips the typed-interface checklist item
risks.mitigation: Build a small immutable record (read-model DTO) in the vet package mapping each specialty to its ordered holder full names, and add a List of it to the Model

notes: primary_paths deliberately diverge from the prd-entry file_targets on two points, both resolving the design questions the PRD hop flagged: (1) file_targets named SpecialtyRepository.java — dropped, because the derive-from-vets decision means no store read is needed (see the ADR); (2) file_targets named VetController.java — replaced by a new SpecialtyController, which matches the prd-entry's own SpecialtyControllerTests test class and keeps VetController focused. Full name is 'given name first' per acceptance criterion 2 (firstName + ' ' + lastName), from Vet extends Person. No conflict with NG-2 (read-only, no management) or the deletion/visit-amendment non-goal ADR. Not foundational (all durable-memory foundations present), not refactor-first (existing VetRepository and Vet.getSpecialties suffice). IDE semantic oracle not available on this dispatch; code claims verified via Read of the vet package and templates. DOC-SYNC FOLLOW-UP (post-implementation): add a SpecialtyController row to system-design.md Contracts (Implements REQ-SPC-001) and a one-line current-state note that the specialty directory reads specialties via the vet aggregate rather than a SpecialtyRepository, back-linked to the new ADR — deferred here because system-design.md carries current state only and the code does not yet exist. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No user input reaches SpecialtyController: fixed /specialties.html GET mapping with a Model-only handler, no request params or path variables to inject through
All template output rendered via th:text (Thymeleaf auto-escaping); no th:utext and no user-controlled SpEL, so no stored/reflected XSS on specialty names or holder names
Data source is the cached VetRepository.findAll() read path; SpecialtyView is an immutable record with a defensive List.copyOf, no state mutation and no serialization sink
No new data exposure: specialty names and veterinarian full names are already public on the existing vet list page; no PII or credentials surfaced
No dependencies added or changed by this slice; no new supply-chain surface

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyControllerTests uses @MockitoBean on VetRepository and Mockito BDD-style given() stubs. CLAUDE.md and the code-quality-review checklist state no mocks and no Mockito. The identical pattern exists in VetControllerTests (grep-confirmed), making this consistent-with-codebase, but the no-mocks principle predates both. Whether @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean is an accepted narrow exception for MVC slice tests — or whether the slice tests should be replaced with full-context integration tests — is a test-design question the test-reviewer should rule on.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyController is package-private and uses constructor injection without @Autowired, mirroring VetController exactly
SpecialtyView is a correctly shaped immutable record with a defensive List.copyOf() in its compact constructor and no mutable state
TreeMap keying on specialty name gives free alphabetical ordering without an explicit sort step; the Comparator for holders by last-then-first name is named and scoped correctly
directory() is a pure query method under 20 lines; holdersBySpecialtyName is a descriptive local variable name
@GetMapping path /specialties.html matches the acceptance criterion; the model attribute name specialties and the view name specialties/specialtyList are consistent
specialtyList.html reuses existing message keys #{specialties}, #{name}, #{vets} — no new i18n keys introduced, mitigating the REQ-LANG-002 build risk named in the design-block
Test names follow the BDD should-convention; aVet() is a readable factory method; @SuppressWarnings(unchecked) is scoped precisely to the one method that requires it
The format check task (checkJavaFormat) is not present in this Gradle build — verified by ./gradlew tasks — so no format findings; build-pass record confirms the check gate passed

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: @MockitoBean on VetRepository stubs an internal Spring Data JPA interface in a new test file. The testing brief (§ Mocking Policy) states new tests must prefer real implementations; a framework stub is a conscious exception only when neither a real implementation nor a hand-written double fits. VetRepository can be served by the real H2 in-memory database via @SpringBootTest, making the exception unjustified for this new class. The existing VetControllerTests.java uses the same pattern but is grandfathered; SpecialtyControllerTests is not.

All four test method names are missing the required the prefix. The testing brief (§ Test Naming) specifies the school as the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. Methods should be theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowHoldersByFullNameGivenNameFirst, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty.
findings.fix: Rename each method by prepending the: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowHoldersByFullNameGivenNameFirst, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty.

findings.description: No test covers the empty-vet-list boundary: when findAll() returns an empty list the page should render with zero specialty rows without error. The testing brief (§ Boundary Testing) requires an empty-input case. Without it a NullPointerException or template rendering error on an empty collection would go undetected.

No test exercises the holder tie-break ordering (lastName then firstName). The setup has no two vets sharing the same last name, so a regression from lastName+firstName ordering to lastName-only sorting would leave all existing tests passing. Add two holders with the same last name to one specialty in the setup and assert their relative order to pin the tiebreak. PRD edge case 1 requires stable order.

specialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage fires two HTTP requests in one test body (mockMvc.perform at line 95, then renderDirectory() at line 101) and asserts two unrelated concerns: absence of the pagination model attribute and the specialty count. This is two acts in one test, violating the four-phase structure. The count assertion also uses a bare literal 3 rather than a value derived from the setup data. Recommended fix: assert only attributeDoesNotExist(totalPages) in this test; the three-specialty count is already pinned by containsExactly in specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName.

approved_aspects: All four PRD acceptance criteria have dedicated test cases with targeted assertions
Specialty ordering verified via containsExactly with alphabetical expectation, pinning the TreeMap sort key
Holder full-name format verified with a concrete SpecialtyView record comparison confirming given-name-first layout
The omit-no-specialty-holder criterion is verified via flatExtracting and doesNotContain — a regression adding James Carter to the directory would fail the test
URL reachability confirmed: every test performs GET /specialties.html and expects status 200
100% line coverage on SpecialtyController, SpecialtyView, and Specialty
aVet() factory method used throughout — construction is not scattered as raw constructor calls
AssertJ fluent assertions used correctly throughout: containsExactly, contains, flatExtracting, doesNotContain, hasSize, attributeDoesNotExist
No phase comments or narration comments in test bodies

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Finding 1 resolved: @MockitoBean replaced by hand-written InMemoryVetRepository static nested class implementing VetRepository, backed by a mutable List, registered via @Import. No Mockito imports in the file. The store(Vet...) method gives each test full control over the roster. This satisfies the Mocking Policy (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: prefer hand-written simple implementations); the WebMvcTest/@MockMvc stack is the one sanctioned framework boundary stand-in per the brief.

Finding 2 resolved: all six test methods carry the required the prefix — theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowHoldersByFullNameGivenNameFirst, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderTiedHoldersByGivenName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderNoRowsGivenAnEmptyRoster, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty — consistent with the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school.

Finding 3 resolved: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderNoRowsGivenAnEmptyRoster calls vets.store() (empty) and asserts assertThat(directory).isEmpty(). A regression that throws NPE or returns a non-empty model on an empty roster fails this test.

Finding 4 resolved: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderTiedHoldersByGivenName stores Helen Leary then Anna Leary under radiology and asserts containsExactly ordering [Anna Leary, Helen Leary]. A regression from lastName+firstName sort to lastName-only sort would leave the order nondeterministic and fail this assertion.
Finding 5 resolved: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage asserts only model().attributeDoesNotExist(totalPages) — single concern, no bare literal 3, no second HTTP request.
InMemoryVetRepository.findAll(Pageable) throws UnsupportedOperationException with a descriptive message, documenting the no-paging contract at the seam rather than silently returning null.
Six tests pass: 6/6, 0 failures, 0 skipped (XML report verified).
AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout; aVet() factory method covers all construction; no phase comments.

author: change-grader
summary: add read-only specialty directory derived from veterinarians

blast_radius.note: Purely additive (zero deletions): two new prod files plus a template in the vet package, one test file, and four doc updates. No sensitive paths, no shared code touched, one new read-only GET endpoint.

semantic_surprise.note: Diff does exactly what described. TreeMap gives alphabetical specialty order, holders sorted lastName-then-firstName and rendered firstName-lastName; vets with no specialty never enter the inner loop so they are omitted; empty roster yields empty list. No inverted operator, boundary, or hidden behavior found.

test_adequacy.note: Six tests assert real outcomes (containsExactly, full SpecialtyView equality) and cover the empty-roster and same-last-name tie-break boundaries the first-round test review demanded; a lastName-only regression would fail the tie-break test. Hand-written in-memory double, no Mockito.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers approve with empty findings in the final round. Round-1 changes_requested items (Mockito, missing boundaries, PRD/system-design links) were all resolved and re-approved cleanly; no lingering caveat, escalate, or unresolved bar_clause remains.

scope_deviation.note: Stays within the requirement surface. The primary-paths divergence from file_targets (no SpecialtyRepository, new SpecialtyController) is a documented design decision resolving the PRD-flagged source-of-truth open question, recorded in an ADR. build_retries=0, consultations=0, one design revision that is the deferred doc-sync.

rationale: Contained, purely additive read-only page whose code matches its description exactly; the boundary logic (omission, alphabetical and tie-break ordering) is directly pinned by real tests, and all four reviewers approved cleanly after resolving round-1 findings. Confirm and merge; a fast read of SpecialtyController.directory() is sufficient.
